claim: Vienna's Café Central, in the Palais Ferstel, opened 1876 and was the meeting place of Trotsky, Freud, Altenberg, Herzl and Zweig; it closes March 2026 for renovation reopening autumn 2026.
quote: The café was opened in 1876 and became a key meeting place of the Viennese intellectual scene... Café Central will be closed from March 16, 2026 due to a comprehensive renovation... expected to reopen in autumn 2026.

claim: Café Central occupies the ground floor of Palais Ferstel, a former bank and stock-market building, and counted Altenberg, Herzl, Adler, Hofmannsthal, Loos, Zweig, Polgar and Trotsky among its regulars.
quote: occupies the ground floor of the Palais Ferstel, a former Bank and Stockmarket Building... Key regulars included Peter Altenberg, Theodor Herzl, Alfred Adler, Hugo von Hofmannsthal, Adolf Loos, Stefan Zweig, Alfred Polgar and Leon Trotsky.

claim: Prague's U Fleků brewpub is documented from 1499, has brewed continuously over 500 years, and seats 1200 guests across eight historic halls and a garden, serving a single 13-degree dark lager.
quote: The first written document dates back to 1499 when the house was bought by maltster Vit Skremenec... one of few breweries in Central Europe which has been brewing continuously for over 500 years... 1200 seats in eight halls and in a garden.

claim: U Fleků is named after 18th-century brewer Flekovsky, sits on medieval Gothic foundations, and its halls have hosted figures from Czech kings to Franz Kafka.
quote: In 1762, the brewery began to prosper under the ownership of a brewer named Flekovsky, which the brewery is still named after... eight historic halls, a medieval courtyard and interiors that have hosted everyone from Czech kings to Franz Kafka.

claim: Budapest's New York Café opened 1894, was dubbed the most beautiful café in the world, became the hub of Hungarian literary life, and was restored in 2006; it sits in the Anantara New York Palace hotel.
quote: the birth of the most beautiful cafe in the world... soon became the center of literary and artistic life... favorite place of rendezvous of artists, writers and poets... Ferenc Molnar even wrote his famous novel The Paul Street Boys right here.

claim: Budapest's Gundel was founded 1894 when Károly Gundel turned a City Park inn into Hungary's most prestigious restaurant; it has over 130 years of history and represented Hungary at the 1939 New York World's Fair.
quote: Karoly Gundel transformed a humble inn in Budapest's City Park into a prestigious dining establishment... more than 130 years of history... became the official restaurant of the Hungarian pavilion of the World Exhibition in New York.

claim: Berlin's Clärchens Ballhaus opened 1913, is the last survivor of some 900 Berlin ballrooms, was renamed after widow Clara Bühler took it over when her husband died in WWI, and is a protected cultural monument.
quote: of the once 900 such ballrooms in Berlin, it is the only one remaining... after Clara's husband died in the First World War, she took the reins of the house and renamed it with her nickname Clarchens Ballhaus... survived two world wars and five systems of government.

claim: Clärchens Ballhaus first opened 13 September 1913 as Bühler's Ballhaus in the rear building of Auguststrasse 24/25 and holds protected Berliner Kulturdenkmal status.
quote: Clarchens Ballhaus first opened on September 13, 1913... Fritz Buhler and his wife Clara Buhler opened Buhler's Ballhaus in the rear building of Auguststrasse 24/25... protected status as Berliner Kulturdenkmal.

claim: Athens' Diporto is a basement taverna in business since 1887 with no sign and no menu, two doors (diporto = two doors) behind the Varvakios market, serving unchanged dishes like gigantes beans.
quote: Diporto is a basement level taverna in business since 1887 with no identifying signage or menu and two modest doors (diporto= two doors) for entry.

claim: Diporto sits in the basement of a 150-year-old neoclassical building, has a cult status among Greeks, and is where lyricist Lefteris Papadopoulos wrote songs over a plate of chickpeas.
quote: the basement of a 150-year-old neoclassical building in the center of Athens... cult-like status among Greeks... where Lefteris Papadopoulos sat when he wrote the lyrics to famous Greek songs while eating a plate of chickpeas with rice.
